title: Cochlear synaptopathy and audiometric measures from human temporal-bone cases of sensorineural hearing loss
text:
Project 2 Public Health Relevance
 The ear damage that underlies the hearing impairments cannot be imaged in living humans.
The only way to reveal the patterns of cellular degeneration is by the evaluation of autopsy
specimens. This Project will determine the extent of damage to nerve fibers and sensory cells in
the inner ears of patients with several of the most common forms of acquired hearing loss.
Since therapeutics to regenerate nerves and sensory cells in a damaged inner ear are on the
horizon, understanding the damage patterns, and how they relate to the audiometric profiles in
the same patients, is key to diagnosis and the selection of subjects for clinical trials.

title: Targeting neuroblastoma cell state plasticity
text:
PROJECT 2 NARRATIVE
Distinct adrenergic (ADR) and mesenchymal (MES) epigenetic states exist in NB, likely contributing to therapy
resistance. We discovered that the MES state is associated with impaired responses to the immunotherapy
dinutuximab, an FDA-approved antibody directed against GD2, a glycolipid on the surface of NB cells, and that
the lysine methyl transferase EZH2 and the scaffolding protein MEN1 (menin) both regulate cell-surface GD2
levels in NB. Our proposal tests chromatin modifying compounds, including clinical inhibitors of EZH2 and menin,
hypothesizing that these agents will transdifferentiate MES NB models into an ADR-like state, thereby increasing
expression of targets critical to both small molecule inhibitors and to immunotherapies, leading to enhanced
responses, meeting the NIH mission of improving patient outcomes.

title: Single-Construct Gene Therapy For Enhanced Heart Repair
text:
Heart failure remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide and, despite substantial investments, continues
to be an unmet medical need. Cardiac reprogramming (CR), which transforms fibroblasts into beating
cardiomyocyte-like cells, offers a promising approach for heart regeneration; however, the low efficiency of
current protocols hinders clinical translation. This application aims to develop a single-construct gene therapy to
enhance CR and promote heart repair post-injury.

title: The peripheral mechanisms underlying mechanical itch
text:
Chronic itch is a distressing condition that impacts millions around the globe. Despite significant advancements
in understanding the neurobiology of acute itch, the deeper cellular and molecular mechanisms driving chronic
itch are still not well-understood. The proposed work will identify novel cellular and molecular mechanisms
underlying acute mechanical itch and the transition to chronic itch, which will facilitate the development of new
management strategies to substantially improve the lives of those living with chronic itch.

title: Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology Operations Center
text:
The Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology seeks to reduce the impact of cancer on people by uniting a broad
community of scientists and clinicians from many disciplines, committed to discovering, validating, and
disseminating effective strategies for the prevention and treatment of cancer. The Alliance aims to continue its
mission into the next grant cycle of generating practice-changing research that directly and favorably impacts
the lives of cancer patients everywhere.

title: Discovering mechanisms of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in cell-type and cellular subtypes of multiple metabolic tissues
text:
Prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is growing globally due to the
concomitant, fast increasing obesity rates. Recent studies have identified two types of MASLD, one that
manifests into more severe liver disease (“liver MASLD”) and another that is primarily associated with CVD
(“systemic MASLD”), suggesting multiple distinct mechanisms and pathways in the pathogenesis of MASLD.
By leveraging multi-omics data from three key human metabolic tissues, we will improve understanding of
MASLD mechanisms by elucidating 1) cell-type level key trans regulators of MASLD genes and 2) cis
regulatory variants and their target genes underlying the two types of MASLD.

title: Functional Genomic Interrogation of Autism Spectrum Disorder Genetic Risk on Microglia-Neuronal Interactions
text:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a highly heritable, heterogenous neurodevelopmental disorder affecting 1 in
36 children, and while functional genomic analysis of post-mortem cortex from donors diagnosed with ASD
reveals activation of microglia, there is little known about microglial activity in ASD during fetal brain development.
This project aims to transcriptionally, functionally, and morphologically characterize the impact of ASD risk gene
mutations on the patterns of microglial activation, using stem cell (SC) derived microglia combined with 3-
dimensional SC cortical spheroids. These studies will identify potential mechanisms of pathophysiology of neuro-
immune dysregulation in ASD and will untangle the effects of genetic risk versus the effects of cell-cell
interactions on microglial activation.

title: How do pancreatic cancers remodel the tumor microenvironment to facilitate lethal metastatic outgrowth?
text:
Understanding how pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remodels its tumor microenvironment (TME) to
rapidly advance its metastatic outgrowth is of great importance to public health because there is critical need
for new therapeutic strategies to target this lethal disease. Deciphering how fibroinflammatory changes
contribute to the loss of primary PDAC’s hallmark fibrous, immune cell-rich “desmoplastic” stroma upon
metastatic progression is of vital importance because it may uncover how metastatic PDACs compose its
poorly fibrotic, immune-cell deplete stroma to support disease progression. This is significantly relevant to the
NCI’s mission because understanding mechanisms that govern primary versus metastatic PDAC TME will
inform new treatment methods to better serve PDAC patients.

title: Exploring the mechanism of chemosensory detection of threatening kairomones and associated behavioral responses
text:
The proposed research will investigate the chemosensory and behavioral mechanisms in mice associated with
the detection and perception of threatening predatory chemosignals. Chemosensation plays an important role
in human well-being, including detecting dangers, food preferences, alcohol consumption, maternal bonding,
and lifespan. Investigating how chemosensation contributes to social behavior can help us understand the
human brain better and provide important insights that can improve the well-being of humans with
chemosensation dysfunction and neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Antigenic determinants of asthma-associated allergens for design of immunotherapy
text:
IgE sensitization to indoor allergens is associated with development of asthma, a disease that affects 26 million
people in the U.S. Monoclonal IgE antibodies specific for asthma-associated allergens will be isolated from
allergic symptomatic subjects as they occur in vivo, to analyze IgE antibody epitopes on mite, cat, and dog
allergens and their associated IgE antibody repertoire. The goal is to elucidate the importance of the intrinsic
properties of these allergens on their role in causing allergic disease, and to produce hypoallergenic mutants
that will be tested for B and T cell reactivity, to generate information that will facilitate a rational design of
allergy vaccines.

title: FLASH-CAR-T radioimmunotherapy in pediatric brain tumor
text:
Immunotherapy has faced significant challenges in treating brain tumors. The goals of this project
are to understand the radiation effects and to develop new combination radioimmunotherapy
approaches for pediatric brain tumors.

title: Multiplexed nanoparticle delivery to increase CRISPR/Cas gene editing for enhanced cancer therapy
text:
Therapeutic application of CRISPR/Cas in solid tumors is currently limited by the stiff and fibrotic tumor
microenvironment that acts as a barrier to nanoparticle uptake. In this grant application, we propose a unique
combination of siRNA-mediated gene silencing of focal adhesion kinase (FAK, a key modulator of tumor
extracellular matrix (ECM)) and CRISPR-mediated gene editing (deletion) of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-
L1, a brake that blocks cancer immunotherapy), via an all-in-one Selective ORgan Targeting (SORT) lipid
nanoparticle (LNP) approach. Outcomes of this work will include elucidation of the fundamental mechanisms
how and why FAK inhibition improves LNP uptake and gene editing, optimized Liver and Lung SORT LNP
formulations for multiplexed siRNA + Cas9 mRNA + sgRNA delivery, and therapeutic benefit in orthotopic and
genetically engineered mouse models of cancer, ultimately revealing a new strategy to enable CRISPR therapies
in solid tumors.

title: Investigating the roles of VEGFR1 in angiogenesis of the allantois and placenta
text:
The mammalian placenta and its precursor, the allantois, are vital for nutrient and gas exchange between the
fetal and maternal circulation. Proper vascular development of these extraembryonic tissues supports fetal
growth, yet the molecular players that drive angiogenesis of the allantois and placenta have not yet been
elucidated. The proposed studies will investigate the contrasting roles of VEGFR1 in angiogenesis of the
allantois and placental vasculature, uncovering a novel signaling function for this key receptor in vascular
development.

title: DNA nanotechnology and synthetic biology for AI-supported detection and precision therapeutics
text:
The proposed paper-based tests will enable rapid screening of a pathogen infection through
visual inspection while the mobile app-facilitated data analysis and wireless communication will prevent the risk
of disease transmission through early detection. The machine-learning supported detection technology enables
diagnostic through tissue analysis, however, it can be used for other public health-related challenges, i.e.,
detection of food-borne pathogens in consumable products. The DNA-hydrogel platform can be used as drug
cargo which releases its content for treatment when the disease-causing pathogen is detected.

title: Research Software Engineer Career Award to Develop Open Science Tools for Environmental Health
text:
This proposal seeks support for Michelle Audirac, as she advances her career in research
software engineering to advance data science and transform environmental health research.
Audirac is a Senior Data Science Specialist and is currently playing a pivotal role, leading data
science engineering and research software efforts in several NIH-funded research programs
focused on studying the impact of environmental and extreme weather exposures on health.
Audirac's proposed research aims to foster the creation of scalable, interoperable research
software, driving critical advancements in environmental health research.

title: Ocular Surface Functions of KLF4 and KLF5
text:
Ocular surface disorders are among the most common reasons for a visit to an ophthalmologist in the world
and are frequently due to abnormal growth and function of the corneal epithelial cells. The research proposed
here will identify the molecular factors and pathways important for normal growth and function of corneal
epithelial cells, and their deficiencies that lead to sight-threatening diseases such as pterygium and ocular
surface squamous neoplasia that if untreated cause corneal blindness.

title: Dynamics and mechanisms of filovirus envelop glycoproteins
text:
Research into Ebola virus infection has yielded therapeutic antibodies and an approved vaccine. But an
expanded treatment repertoire, which exploits new targets is needed to combat the increasing frequency and
severity of Ebola outbreaks. Completion of the multidisciplinary research proposed here will provide mechanistic
insights into filovirus entry and the viral and host targets that could be exploited with novel therapies and
immunogens.

title: AMPA Receptor Function at Interneuron Synapses
text:
Calcium-permeable glutamate receptors are important for brain development and plasticity, and have been
implicated in many disease states. The goal of this project is to understand the biophysical properties of
calcium-permeable glutamate receptors to expand our knowledge of activity-dependent brain development and
plasticity.

title: Pulmonary and pancreatic response to cystic fibrosis modulator therapy in young children
text:
Highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT) has recently become available for the majority of
people with cystic fibrosis (CF). The effects on lung function can be quite dramatic but the effects
on the pancreas are minimal, probably due to the fact that the pancreas undergoes fibrosis which
is complete by the teen years. In this study, we aim to uncover novel insights into the biological
mechanisms driving the natural history of disease progression in CF by revealing how the newest
HEMT, Trikafta™, improves pulmonary and pancreatic function in young children, an age with
great potential for growth and repair.

title: Dynamic DNA Modifications in Brain and Diseases
text:
As an intermediate regulatory paradigm between DNA sequences and gene expression,
epigenetic mechanisms can exert substantial influence on normal brain function. Increasing
evidence indicates that multiple neurodevelopmental, neurodegenerative, and psychiatric
disorders are caused, at least in part, by aberrant epigenetic modifications. We will integrate
various disciplines to understand dynamic DNA modifications during neurodevelopment and
aging as well as their dysregulation in the pathogenesis of human diseases.
